reasons: The rule is protective: it caps Vendor audit rights against us. The cited paragraphs (Section 3 use restrictions, Section 20 general matters, and the p0114 escrow examination right that runs in Sparkling's favour) contain no Vendor right to audit, inspect or verify Customer usage and no system-access language, so the document sits better than the preferred position.

Classifying as compliant with no redline and no comment is the correct handling — raising this as 'missing' would invite audit language into a contract that currently gives the Vendor none, which would harm our position.
The failed deterministic check ('audit frequency limited') is explained by the total absence of an audit clause rather than by an unlimited audit right; it is not evidence of a deviation here.
No actionable proposal is required for a compliant finding, and none was made; the redline is identical to the original text as expected.
